questions.question:
Direction: Out of the two bar graphs provided below, one shows the amounts (Rs. In Lakhs) invested by a company in purchasing raw materials over the years and the other shows the values (Rs. In Lakhs) of finished goods sold by the company over the years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ddf6b7261e865aad7dc58a76e2548b23665680ce74d29f2fd1978de130f07b97.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f0366ad1232648815be5ec36f2c885a5ec345508fd9d6bd8930920d4f3754afa.png] 

What was the difference between the average amount invested in raw materials during 1997 to 2000 and the average value of sales of finished goods during the same period 1997 to 2000?
questions.solution:
Average amount invested in raw materials during 1997 to 2000 = (375 + 330 + 525 + 420) /4 = 1650/4 = 412.5

Average amount of sales of finished goods during 1997 to 2000 = (500 + 400 + 600 + 460) /4 = 1960/4 = 490

Required difference = 490 – 412.5 = 77.5

questions.question: If 10 men can complete a piece of work in 12 days by working 7 hours a day, then in how many days can 14 men do the same work by working 6 hours a day?
questions.solution:
As we know,

Total work = M × H × D

M = Number of person, H = Number of the hour, D = Number of days,

Let the number of days be d, then

According to the question

10 × 12 × 7 = 14 × d × 6

D = (10 × 12 × 7)/(14 × 6)

D = 10 days

questions.question: What is the difference between the average percentage of marks in vernacular of the districts (D1, D2, D4) and (D3, D5)?
questions.solution:
Total marks of D1, D2 and D4 = 80 + 70 + 75 = 225

Average marks of D1, D2 and D4 = 225/3 = 75

75 means 75% because the maximum marks of each subject are 100.

Total marks of D3 and D5 = 50 + 55 = 105

Average marks of D1 and D5 = 105/2 = 52.5

Average percentage of D1 and D5 = 52.5%

Required difference = 75% – 52.5% = 22.5%

questions.question: PQRS is a rectangle. T is a point on PQ such that RTQ is an isosceles triangles and PT = 5QT. If the area of ΔRTQ is 12√3 sq.cm, then the area of the rectangle PQRS is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/93a5e7e6ff6b5804c5543da8298c647ade9f879df2115fb19b9230f89ab3016d.png] 

Given,

PT = 5QT

PT : QT = 5 : 1

Let the ratio of PT : QT be 5x : x.

PQ = PT + QT

PQ = 5x + x

PQ = 6x

PQ = RS [PQRS is a rectangle]

RS = 6x

In rectangle PQRS, there are three triangle ΔPST, ΔRTQ and ΔSTR

Area of ΔRTQ = 1/2 × Base × height

½ × x × RQ = 12√3

RQ = (12√3 × 2) /x

RQ = 24√3/x

Area of rectangle PQRS = ar ΔRTQ + ar ΔPST + ar ΔSTR

Area of rectangle PQRS = (1/2) × QT × RQ + (1/2) × PT × RQ + (1/2) × SR × RQ

Area of rectangle PQRS = (1/2) × RQ [QT + PT + SR] = (1/2) × (24√3/x) [x + 5x + 6x]

Area of rectangle PQRS = [12√3/x] × [12x] = 144√3 sq.cm

questions.question: 4 boys from school A and 6 boys from school B together can set up an exhibition in 5 days, which 5 boys from school A and 10 boys from school C together can do in 4 days or 3 boys from school B and 4 boys from school C together can do in 10 days. Then how many boys from school A can set up the exhibition in one day?
questions.solution:
As we know,

Total work of first group = total work of second group = total work of third group

(4A + 6B) × 5 = (5A + 10C) × 4 = (3B + 4C) × 10

(4A + 6B) × 5 = (3B + 4C) × 10

4A + 6B = 6B + 8C

4A = 8C

A : C = 8 : 4

A : C = 2 : 1 ...(1)

Again,

(5A + 10C) × 4 = (3B + 4C) × 10

20A + 40C = 30B + 40C

20A = 30B

A : B = 30 : 20

A : B = 3 : 2 ...(2)

From equation (1) and equation (2)

A : B : C : = 6 : 4 : 3

Total work = (4A + 6B) × 5 = (4 × 6 + 6 × 4) × 5 = 48 × 5 = 240

Let number of students from school A complete the work be x.

x × 6 = 240

x = 240/6

x = 40

questions.question: The two parallel sides of a trapezium are 27 cm and 13 cm respectively. If the height of the trapezium is 8 cm, then what is its area in m²?

questions.question: A wheel has diameter 84 cm, then how far does the wheel go (in metres) in 16 revolutions? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Radius of the wheel = 84/2 = 42 cm

Circumference of the wheel = 2 πr = 2 × (22/7) × 42 = 264 cm

Distance covered by the wheel in 1 revolution = Circumference of the wheel

Distance covered by the wheel in 16 revolution = 16 × 264 = 4224 cm = 4224/100 m

= 42.24 m

questions.question: A person has to travel a distance of 30 km he finds that he has covered 5/6 of the distance in 3 hours and 20 minutes. What is his speed in km/h?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

3 hr 20 min = 3 + 20/60 = 3 + 1/3 = 10/3

Total distance = 30 km.

5/6th of the distance = 30 × (5/6) = 25 km

Speed of the person = 25/(10/3) = 7.5 km/hr

**∴ Speed is 7.5 km/hr**

questions.question: The height of a right circular cone is 35 cm and the area of its curved surface is four times the area of its base. What is the volume of the cone (in 10⁻³m³ and correct up to three-decimal places)?
questions.solution:
Height of the cone h = 35 cm 

As we know,

Volume of cone = (1/3) πr²h

Curved surface area of cone = πrl

Base area of cone = πr²

According to the question

4 × πr² = πrl

l = 4r

As we know,

l² = r² + h²

(4r)² = r² + 35²

16r² – r² = 1225

15r² = 1225

r² = 1225/15

Volume of the cone = (1/3) × πr²h = (1/3) × (22/7) × (1225/15) × 35 = 2994 cm³

= 2994 cm³ = 2994/10⁶ m³ = 2994 × 10–⁶ m³ = 2.994 × 10–³ m³

questions.question: A pole stands vertically on a road, which goes in the north-south direction. P, Q are two points towards the north of the pole, such that PQ = b, and the angles of elevation of the top of the pole at P, Q are α, β respectively. Then the height of the pole is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab6259a5d920c08c29f8dc220fbadabd3ab93ff1aa38fa8a0ae8b29d885232b3.png] 

Let Height of the pole be h cm.

PQ = b

In ΔABQ

tan β = AB/BQ

tan β = h/BQ

BQ = h/tan β

BQ = h cot β

In Δ ABP

tan α = AB/BP

tan α = h/BP

BP = h/tan α

BP = h cot α

BQ = BP + PQ

h cot β = h cot α + b

h (cot β - cot α) = b

h = b/(cot β - cot α)

questions.question: A clock tower stands at the crossing of two roads which point in the north-south and the east-west directions. P, Q, R and S are points on the road due north, east, south and west respectively, where the angles of elevation of the top of the tower are respectively, α, β, γ and δ. Then (PQ/RS)² is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c282a94b3d467dc422b2e5f4812036d824ab23a3597cdc77d88b956744d6f5a.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/301e4cb646d09665832cf945a231eb026b9b45d30ff4d0e03c13811ef60ae9bf.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c58c679ed31d07c8b2c647c54c841ccbc2e07758f95d70a418fd970260a35a11.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f418dd91db632cb1cdf3db31db3e187595f9c5cafa02ff30e1849aa93d6fa147.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dd1763eb427ee981bcc4cc91d12619f3d2463688bde80f163c73570b31656eeb.png] 

Let K is the point on the top of the tower and the height of the clock tower OK be h cm

OK is perpendicular to PR and SQ.

In ΔPOK,

tan α = OK/OP

OP = h/tan α

OP = h cot α

Similarly,

In ΔQOK

tan β = OK/OQ

OQ = h/tan β

OQ = h cot β

In ΔPOQ, OP is perpendicular to OQ, then

PQ² = OP² + OQ²

PQ² = h² cot² α + h² cot² β

PQ² = h² (cot² α + cot² β)

Similarly,

RS² = h² (cot² γ + cot² δ)

Now,

(PQ/RS)² = [h² (cot² α + cot² β)]/[h² (cot² γ + cot² δ)]

(PQ/RS)² = (cot² α + cot² β)/(cot² γ + cot² δ)

questions.question: Three pipes, A, B, C can fill an empty cistern in 2, 3 and 6 hours respectively. They are opened together. After what time should B be closed, so that the cistern gets filled in exactly 1 hr 15 min?
questions.solution:
1 hr 15 min = 1 + 1/4 = 5/4 hr

Total work = 6 unit

Work done by A in 1 hr = 6/2 = 3

Work done by C in 1 hr = 6/6 = 1

Work done by A and C in 5/4 hr = (3 + 1) × 5/4 = 5 unit

Remaining work = 6 – 5 = 1

Pipe B work in 1 hr = 6/3 = 2 unit

Pipe B work in 30 min = 1 unit

So, the pipe should B be closed after 30 min.

4x² + 12xy - 2x + 9y² - 3y - 20 = (ax² + by² + 2hxy + 2gx + 2fy + c)

On comparing

a = 4, h = 6, g = -1, b = 9, f = -3/2 and c = -20

Now,

{(g + f - c)/abh}

{(-1 - 3/2 + 20)/4 × 9 × 6}

{(-2 - 3 + 40)/2}/(4 × 6 × 9)

(35/2)/216

35/432

questions.question: Sudeep invested 1/8 of a certain sum at 5% per annum for two years and 3/5 of the sum of 6% per annum for two years and the remaining at 10% p.a. for two years. If the total interest received is Rs. 1,674, then the total sum invested is:
questions.solution:
As we know,

Simple Interest = PRT/100

Let total sum be Rs. x, then

Remaining part = x - x/8 - 3x/5 = (40x - 5x - 24x)/40 = 11x/40

According to the question

(x × 1/8 × 5 × 2)/100 + (x × 3/5 × 6 × 2)/100 + (x × 11/40 × 10 × 2)/100 = 1674

5x/400 + 36x/500 + 11x/200 = 1674

(25x + 144x + 110x)/2000 = 1674

279x/2000 = 1674

x = 1674 × 2000/279

x = 12000

**Alternate Solution:**

Let total number be 40x, then

As we know,

40x × 1/8 = 5x and 40x × 3/5 = 24x and 40x - 5x - 24x = 11x

According to the question

[2 × (5x × 5 + 24x × 6 + 11x × 10)]/100 = 1674

2 × 279x = 167400

558x = 167400

x = 167400/558

x = 300

Total sum = 40 × 300 = 12000

questions.question: If 0 ≤ θ ≤ 90°, and sec¹⁰⁷ θ + cos¹⁰⁷ θ = 2, then, (sec θ + cos θ) is equal to:

questions.question: I purchase 100 kg of tea and sell it for a profit to the extent of what I would have paid for 40 kg. What is my profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Cost Price = CP, Selling Price = SP

According to the question

100 SP - 100 CP = 40 CP

100 SP = 140 CP

CP : SP = 100 : 140

Profit = 140 - 100 = 40

Profit % = (40/100) × 100 = 40%

questions.question: While tabulation of marks scored in an examination by the students of a class, by mistake the marks scored by one student got recorded as 93 in place of 63, and thereby the average marks increased by 0.5. What was the number of students in the class?
questions.solution:
**Short trick:**

Required number of students = (93 - 63)/0.5 = 30/0.5 = 60

Detailed solution:

Let the total number of students be x and average marks of the students be y, then

According to the question

xy + 93 - 63 = x × (y + 0.5)

xy + 30 = xy + 0.5x

0.5x = 30

x = 30/0.5

x = 60

questions.question: At what percentage rate, compound interest compounded annually for a sum of Rs. 40,000, will amount to Rs. 44,100 in two years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P = 40,000 and A = 44,100 and t = 2 years

**Calculation:**

A = P (1 + r/100)t

⇒ 44,100 = 40,000 (1 + r/100)²

⇒ (1 + r/100)² = 44,100/40,000

⇒ (1 + r/100) = √44,100/40,000

⇒ r/100 = 21/20 - 1

⇒ r/100 = 1/20

⇒ r = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%**

questions.question: The speed of two railway engines is in the ratio 5 : 4. If they move on parallel tracks in the same direction and if the slower engine is ahead of the faster engine by 8 km when the latter starts, then how far will the faster engine have to travel before it overtakes the slower one?
questions.solution:
Speed ratio of two engines is = 5 : 4

Let the speed of the faster engine is 5 km/hr and speed of the slower engines is 4 km/hr

The distance of the two engines = 8 km

Required time to overtake by faster engine = 8/ (5 – 4) = 8 hr

Distance covered by the faster engine in 8 hrs = 5 × 8 = 40 km

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 3 : 5. If eight is added to the first, and seven to the second, then the ratio becomes 2 : 3. What will be the ratio becomes if six is added to each?
questions.solution:
Ratio of two number are = 3x : 5x

According to the question

(3x + 8)/(5x + 7) = 2/3

3 (3x + 8) = 2 (5x + 7)

9x + 24 = 10x + 14

10x - 9x = 24 - 14

x = 10

The first number = 3 × 10 = 30

Second number = 5 × 10 = 50

If 6 is added in each then new ratio = (30 + 6) : (50 + 6) = 36 : 56 = 9 : 14
